summary: Lookout station set up on Black Mountain, Cambridge NH, in 1910 with timberland owners' money; a wooden tower and cabin by 1922; now listed as gone.

facts.design: Disputed: wooden tower with a cabin (1921-22 forestry report) or open tower (FFLA list)
facts.status_note: The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as gone and a hiking blog lists it as no longer standing. No source describes the site today.

events.note: Lookout station established; paid for by the NH Timberland Owners Association
New wooden tower and cabin, per the Biennial Report of the Forestry Commission, 1921-22

evidence.supports: Lookout station established at this point in 1910
evidence.quote: 1910: A lookout station was established at this point.

evidence.supports: Timberland owners association paid for seven 1910 towers, Cambridge Black among them
evidence.quote: The other seven, established on mountains Magalloway, Sugarloaf, Signal, Cambridge Black, Pine, Carrigain, and Osceola, were paid for by the NH Timberland Owners Association.

evidence.supports: New wooden tower and cabin on Black Mountain in Cambridge by the 1921-22 report
evidence.quote: A new wooden tower and cabin on Black Mountain in Cambridge.

evidence.supports: Association list calls it an open tower and marks it gone
evidence.quote: Cambridge Black Coos 44.63452 -71.09167 Open Tower Gone

evidence.supports: Hiking blog list marks the site as no longer standing
evidence.quote: Cambridge Black - Cambridge 2711 No Longer Standing /Artifacts

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list says open tower, meaning no cab, while the 1921-22 forestry report describes a wooden tower and cabin. The story leaves the form open until a photo or fuller report settles it.

sources.title: You Are Here: NH Fire Towers

notes_for_editor: Four readable sources, none of them a state or federal record. The 1910 and 1922 dates come from the Forest Lookouts page quoting old reports, and NH Family Hikes adds the 1910 owner. The FFLA list says open tower while the 1922 report says cabin; the record shows both descriptions and the story says the form is unsettled. No source on staffing, access, or what remains at the site today; the NH Family Hikes page was read over http because https fails certificate checks. The state fire-tower history PDF returned 403, so it is not used. The 1910 station may not have been a tower at all, and the sources do not say.
